Subject: RE: Equinox: initial demand forecast and latency targets (sizing notes)

Summary from the sizing sync and my back-of-envelope model mapping: 

Assumptions (testable inputs)
- Primary model: rw-extended-13B (quantized 4-bit; seq len: prompt+gen ~180 tokens avg).
- HW candidate: NVIDIA A100-80GB (shared node slab), and an alternate SKU = H100 for lower latency if needed.
- KV cache: effective hit rate ~25% for sessioned flows -> reduces token generation workload.
- Tail behavior: p99 amplification ~2.0x relative to median token compute due to longer completions/events.

Per-GPU throughput estimates (sustained, avg workload)
- rw-extended-13B @ 4-bit on A100-80GB: ~1,050 tokens/sec sustained (single replica baseline for gen path). p95 latency ~220ms, p99 ~470ms (so p99 slightly above target without headroom).
- rw-8B (fallback): ~2,400 tokens/sec sustained, p95 ~140ms, p99 ~230ms.

Sizing logic
1) Steady-state requirement: 1.2M tokens/sec aggregate -> With 25% KV caching, effective tokens to serve = 900k tokens/sec.
2) If each A100 handles 1,050 tps sustained, nominal GPUs = 900k / 1,050 ≈ 857 GPUs.
3) That's the raw compute floor. For redundancy, maintenance, and to absorb p99 amplification and model variance, recommend committed slab = raw floor * 1.35 ≈ 1,157 GPUs.
4) Operational approach: commit 1,200 A100 GPUs in Dedicated (US region) + autoscale pool to 1,600 for launch bursts (burst policy uses pre-provisioned spare capacity + cross-region fallback).

Cost/ops notes and mitigations
- If a single-model approach at 13B is too expensive, hybrid strategy: primary traffic to rw-8B smaller model for stateless short completions and reserve rw-13B for high-quality long-tail queries via model routing (can be prioritized via route-based flags). That reduces committed GPUs materially (estimate ~40% GPU reduction for many chat-first workloads).
- Consider H100s for latency-sensitive slices of traffic (p99 headroom under target). H100s give better p99 but higher per-hour cost. We can model a split: ~10% H100 for the highest SLO lanes, 90% A100 for bulk.

Recommended concrete offer to Equinox
- Commit: 1,200 A100 GPUs (US) as Dedicated pool; burstable to 1,600 via autoscale/overspill and cross-region failover.
- Token allowance (committed): map to monthly tokens = steady-state 1.2M tps * 3600s * 24h * 30d (apply business-hour factor 0.5 for conservative billing) -> ballpark commit = 1.6T tokens / month. Exact number in SOW to be finalized with procurement.
- Operating runbook: canary (5% traffic to new model), graceful fallback to rw-8B at X% if latency degradation or queueing observed, and quick throttle policy for non-authenticated heavy batch jobs.

I'll prepare a short slide with the numbers and sensitivity (1.2M -> 6M burst) and include alternate scenarios (aggressive mixed-model routing vs single-model commitment).

Karthik
Director, Inference Optimization

Liam / procurement team — thanks, and apologies for the dense math in the thread. Quick customer-facing summary and next steps below.

Executive summary (what we recommend)\- Redwood recommends a phased Dedicated commitment for Equinox:
  1) Pilot (Jan-Feb 2027): 150 A100 GPUs reserved (US) to validate real traffic patterns and KV cache impact; measure effective tokens/sec per-GPU and p95/p99 latency with live data.
  2) On successful pilot: scale to a committed slab of 1,200 A100 GPUs (monthly commitment) + autoscale to 1,600 GPUs for planned bursts (product launches).
  3) Traffic strategy: route latency-critical lanes to a small H100 pool (10% of peak) while bulk inference remains on A100 with quantized 13B / 8B hybrid routing to control costs.

Operational safeguards and guarantees\- SLOs: Target 95% <250ms, p99 <450ms. We'll instrument token-level latency reporting and create per-route dashboards during pilot.
- Fallbacks: automated model routing to rw-8B and token-based throttling for non-urgent flows to preserve SLOs for interactive users.
- Runbook: canary deploy, traffic mirroring, warm KV-cache pre-warming for launch windows, and a predefined escalation path to Redwood ops + on-call.

Commercials (ballpark for procurement discussions)
- Committed slab: mapped to an initial token allowance ~1.6T tokens/month (subject to pilot calibration).
- Overage policy: tiered pricing with soft-burst window and prioritized throttling beyond 120% of commit.
- SOW draft attached for review (EQX_SOW_v1.pdf).

Next actions
- Liam: please confirm acceptance of the pilot plan and whether 1/10 — 2/1/2027 windows work for your engineering team for the pilot run.
- Procurement: review attached SOW and we'll iterate; I'll drop the refined GPU/token numbers into the HubSpot deal record (HS-87654321) and circulate a DocuSign SOW link once we align.

Attaching the draft SOW and will follow up with the shorter slide for execs that surfaces the 3 scenarios (low-cost hybrid, baseline single-model, high-availability with H100).

Thanks —
